description: Time-ordered windows and maintenance in PostgreSQL on real timestamps: IMDb release dates and Amazon review timestamps (recovered 2026-11-06): sliding windows ORDER BY ts with ROWS and time-based RANGE frames vs ORDER BY id on the same rows; softavg_ivm under a timestamp-order insert stream with sliding retention vs a random stream with the same statement and row counts.

extension.name: bruce_pg
extension.build_cmd: cargo pgrx install --release --pg-config <server>/bin/pg_config (pgrx 0.18.1; profile.release opt-level=3, lto=fat, codegen-units=1)

server.pg_version: PostgreSQL 17.10 on x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04) 11.4.0, 64-bit

builds_note: `server`/`environment` = the build of the Amazon runs (after softagg-core's B1 bound change); the IMDb runs (window, maint) used the earlier build recorded in `imdb_runs_build`

amazon.source: McAuley-Lab/Amazon-Reviews-2023 raw/review_categories/<cat>.jsonl, streamed by build_amazon_ts.py (2026-11-06) up to the corpus' last line per category; nothing written to disk but amazon_ts.parquet

load.query_text: It’s a great deal for a great price
load.score: float32 inner product (numpy), stored as float8

sources.stackexchange: donfu/oa-stackexchange has no CreationDate / post id (METADATA: answer_score, question_score, tags) -> no timestamps recoverable from the source used
